comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–2027 study guide (p.10–11) explicitly names the main route Klassieke Theologie and its sustained biblical-language sequence. This general theological route is selected independently of UCR fit. The former 35-EC Religie en Samenleving Track 2 was converted from September 2026 into the 30-EC Theologie voor Kerk en Samenleving minor and a variant with language substitutions (p.76); that historical track is not carried forward. The official 2026–2027 full-time course overview fixes the 60/60/60-EC sequence. Its individual credited components are expanded here from the earlier year aggregates, preserving the same ordinary full-language curriculum and 180 EC. The third year retains genuine 30-EC internal/external minor space, seven continuing specialist/formation components and a 10-EC thesis. Missiology is one 7.5-EC module spanning periods C and D; formation entries repeated through the year are counted once. Current programme-page first-year examples are labelled 2025–2026, so the dated 2026–2027 guide and overview govern current formal details. The guide also confirms Christian Ecological Thinking and Theology for Church and Society as available minor directions; they inform UCR candidate concepts without being substituted into the comparator minor.

alternatives.concept: Investigate worldviews, moral agency and cultural meaning through philosophy, literary and mythic traditions, visual culture, historical sources and the social institutions through which beliefs are expressed. This is a related humanities and social-science response to the Theology target, without substituting these methods for Christian doctrine, biblical languages or exegesis.

alternatives.concept: Examine moral responsibility in public life through ethics, political thought, human rights, civic organisations, public communication and ecological justice. alternatives.labelRationale: Moral and political philosophy, human-rights/public law, civil society, communication, environmental justice and sustainability governance form the actual curriculum. Environmental responsibility is supported by several linked courses and projects, rather than a single incidental topic.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: 12 courses (90 EC) differ in each direction. Literary interpretation, archaeological/art-historical study and historical-source research give way to constitutional/international law, peacebuilding, environmental justice, climate communication, sustainability governance and community research. The change follows an evidenced shift from interpreting cultural traditions to ethical judgment and civic/environmental action.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic normalized target names no route. The current 2026–2027 guide identifies Klassieke Theologie as the main route, retaining the full biblical-language sequence and access to the university’s theological master directions. alternativeSelection.assessment: Two complete related-fields programmes are defensible. The closest response studies philosophical and cultural meaning through evidenced humanities and social methods; it does not reproduce the theological core. The second changes the curriculum materially toward public ethics, civic action and ecological responsibility, supported by the current guide’s Church and Society and Christian Ecological Thinking offerings. Historical interest row 12228 is used as public-society direction evidence corroborated by the current minor/variant, not as proof that the old route still exists. Biblical languages/exegesis was assessed independently for a third programme: UCR has literary criticism, myth and stylistics but no biblical Hebrew, New Testament Greek, Old/New Testament exegesis or theological hermeneutics sequence, so those methods cannot be expanded into a complete scriptural-study curriculum. Practical/pastoral theology was assessed separately: sociology of civil society, rhetoric and community projects support civic practice, already included in Alternative 2, but supply no practical-theology, worship, pastoral/diaconal formation or supervised ecclesial practice. A third pastoral curriculum would therefore require unsupported substitutions. Neither rejection is based merely on absence of a professional qualification.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both explicitly introduce philosophical inquiry and argument; UCR covers a broad Western tradition rather than a theological programme foundation.
Both directly examine ethical theories and moral reasoning; UCR does not reproduce the comparator’s Christian theological framing.
Accounts of personhood and the self are an identifiable shared philosophical subject; Philosophy of Mind does not reproduce the whole philosophical-anthropology course.
